methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops in Hampton Roads signal grassroots capability building outside traditional tech hubs, demonstrating distributed peer-to-peer knowledge transfer that could bridge the urban-rural divide if scaled.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents institutional investment in deep AI literacy beyond NoVA, creating regional capacity for workforce transformation rather than shallow tool adoption.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Student analysis explicitly identifies data center concentration in NoVA as exacerbating urban-rural divides, signaling that infrastructure investment alone doesn't distribute capability without intentional equity mechanisms.

signals.title: Virginia needs more technical workers, but it’s stepping away from funding a program to develop them
signals.signal_reading: Defunding the GO TEC technical workforce program serving 49 rural school divisions removes a key pathway for distributed AI-adjacent capability, actively pushing toward concentration rather than distribution.

signals.title: ‘Shaping our future’: Company powering AI data centers invests $50+ million in Henrico, adding 200 jobs - WWBT
signals.signal_reading: A $50M+ data center infrastructure investment with 200 jobs in Henrico deepens Richmond's emerging tech hub status but signals hardware/operations jobs rather than AI development capability that would indicate deep expertise.
